## Why plan now?

You have been here four weeks. Why map out four years?

::: {.nonincremental}
- Some courses are only offered in **fall** or **spring**.
- Prerequisite chains are long. One missed semester can push graduation back a year.
- A minor, research, study abroad, or a co-op all need room in the plan, and room is easiest to make early.
- Your advisor can help you much more when you show up with a plan.
:::

::: {.highlight-box}
**A map is a plan, not a contract.** You will revise it. That is the point.
:::

---

## What is a degree map?

The School of Physics' [4-year plan](https://ballantyne.physics.gatech.edu/FourYearPlans/BS%20PHYS%20Traditional%204%20Yr%20Plan.pdf) with no transfer credit starts like this:

| Semester | Courses | Hours | Running total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fall 2026 | ENGL 1101, MATH 1551, MATH 1553, CHEM 1310, GT 1000 | 15 | 15 |
| Spring 2027 | ENGL 1102, MATH 1552, PHYS 2231, CS 1301, APPH 1040 | 17 | 32 |
| Summer 2027 | *Study abroad? Internship?* | -- | 32 |
| ... | ... | ... | ... |
| Spring 2030 | PHYS 4605, electives | 14 | &ge; 122 |

---

## Anatomy of the Physics B.S.

**122 credit hours** total ([Physics B.S. - General](https://catalog.gatech.edu/programs/physics-general-bs/)).

| Block | Examples |
|---|---|
| Core IMPACTS | ENGL 1101/1102, CS 1301/1371 |
| Field of study | PHYS 2303, PHYS 2304 |
| Upper-level physics | E&M, quantum, thermo |
| Physics / technical electives | PHYS, approved MATH, NRE |
| Free electives | **Anything**: this is where a minor lives |

::: {.highlight-box}
**Applied Physics or Astrophysics?** Same first year, different upper levels. Use your own [4-year plan](https://physics.gatech.edu/academics/undergraduate/requirements).
:::

::: notes
Per-block hours from the catalog (IMPACTS 43, field of study 18, upper-level 32, electives 18, free
15) sum to 126, not 122, so some blocks overlap. The School's 4-year plan sums to 122. Physics and
Applied Physics both have a Business Option and a Physics of Living Systems concentration, each
with its own 4-year plan.
:::

## Prerequisites set the order

Your map is really a set of **chains**. Build the chains first, then fill in around them.

::: {.nonincremental}
- **Math:** MATH 1551 &rarr; 1552 &rarr; 2551 &rarr; 2552
- **Intro physics:** PHYS 2231 &rarr; 2232 &rarr; 2303 / 2304
- **Upper level:** intro physics + math &rarr; 3000-level &rarr; 4000-level
:::

When in doubt, check [Oscar](https://oscar.gatech.edu/).

**Example:** PHYS 3143 Quantum Mechanics I requires (PHYS 2213 or 2304) **and** MATH 2551 **and** MATH 2552 (or equivalent).


::: notes
The 3143 prerequisites are from the School of Physics requirements page (Quantum minor section).
In the 4-year plan, MATH 2552 and PHYS 2304 are both spring of year 2, so QM I lands in fall of
year 3. Taking 2211/2212 instead of 2231/2232 moves two hours to physics/technical electives.
Consider drawing the chain on the board. Check which upper-level courses are offered only once a
year.
:::

---

## Transfer credit counts

AP, IB, dual enrollment, and courses from other schools all go on your map.

::: {.nonincremental}
- List each one and **which requirement it satisfies**.
- Check that it actually shows up in [DegreeWorks](https://degreeworks.gatech.edu/). If it doesn't, find out why **now**.
- More credit is not automatically better. Skipping a course you are shaky on can hurt later in the chain.
- DegreeWorks can have errors where classes that should count, don't. Check with you academic advisor about these.
:::

::: notes
Ask who arrived with MATH 1551 or PHYS 2211 credit. Encourage anyone who placed out of calculus but felt unsure to talk to their advisor before spring registration.
:::

---

## Room for more

Your free and technical electives are where the degree becomes yours.

| Option | How it fits |
|---|---|
| **Minor or certificate** | Physics' minors are 15 hours; up to 6 can double-count toward your major |
| **Undergraduate research** | PHYS 2699 / 4699, at most 9 hours toward the degree (Astrophysics: at most 3 hours of 4699 as an elective) |
| **Internship** | One semester or a summer, full- or part-time |
| **Co-op** | Alternating semesters of full-time work and full-time classes |
| **Study abroad** | A summer program or a full semester away |

::: notes
The School offers minors in Physics (non-physics majors only), Astrophysics (open to Physics and
Applied Physics majors), and Quantum Sciences and Technology (open to all). Research gets its own
lecture on Nov. 20. The Montgomery Machining Mall tour on Sept. 25 is also a
good fit for students who want to build things in lab.
:::

## Study abroad: the deadlines are earlier than you think

::: {.nonincremental}
- **Oct. 12:** [Georgia Tech Europe, Spring 2027](https://atlas.gatech.edu/_portal/tds-program-brochure?programid=10215). First-years can apply; admission is conditional on your first-semester GPA (2.5 minimum).
- **Dec. 1 -- Feb. 15:** most **Summer 2027** programs. This is the most realistic option for first-years.
- **Feb. 1, 2027:** most exchange programs for Fall 2027 / the academic year.
:::

Search programs in [ATLAS](https://atlas.gatech.edu/_portal/program-discovery). If US Citizen, make sure you have a [Passport](https://ea.oie.gatech.edu/apply-us-passport).

::: {.highlight-box}
**Coming up:** [Education Abroad 101: Faculty-Led Programs](https://ea.oie.gatech.edu/event/2026/09/22/education-abroad-101-faculty-led-programs), Tue., Sept. 22 &middot; [Education Abroad Fair](https://ea.oie.gatech.edu/event/2026/10/20/education-abroad-fair), Tue., Oct. 20
:::

::: notes
Deadlines were pulled from ATLAS on Sept. 16 (see planning/lecture-04-study-abroad-deadlines.md).
Re-check the GTE Spring deadline the morning of class. Remind them a passport can take weeks:
https://ea.oie.gatech.edu/apply-us-passport

## Starting your map

::: {.nonincremental}
1. Open the [template](https://sites.gatech.edu/gt1000-textbook/wp-content/uploads/sites/658/2017/07/Degree-Map.xlsx) and your DegreeWorks audit.
2. Enter your **transfer credit** and your **Fall 2026** schedule.
3. Lay out the **math** and **physics** chains through graduation.
4. *Optional:* Mark time for research, study abroad, an internship, or a co-op.
5. Fill the rest with core and electives. Check each semester's hours.
:::

---

## Before you submit

Due **Sept. 25, 11:59 PM ET** &middot; [Degree Map assignment](../assignments/deliverables/degree-map.qmd)

::: {.nonincremental}
- Every semester through your expected graduation.
- Every required course appears, and prerequisites come first.
- Transfer credit listed with what each one satisfies.
- Minor courses, if any.
- Where study abroad, research, an internship, or a co-op could fit.
- Credit hours per semester, a running total, and &ge; 122 at the end.
- One PDF named `Lastname-Firstname-Degree-Map.pdf`.
:::

::: notes
This map is also the starting point for the advising meeting assignment due Oct. 30, so a careful job now saves work later.
:::
